newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AHK to axe surcharge but up ex-Europe cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: AHK to axe surcharge but up ex-Europe cargo rates.

text.p: Air Hong Kong (AHK) will drop its cargo fuel surcharge from May 1, said the carrier's European general manager, Marcel Buelens.
Equivalent to 10 U.S. cents per kg, this was introduced last November.
The all-cargo carrier, 75 percent owned by Cathay Pacific Airways, is then looking to increase its cargo rates ex-Continental Europe for the second time this year from June 1, he added.
Increases will probably be in the region of five percent, he said, adding that this will depend on market conditions.
AHK last inreased its ex-Continental European rates to all destinations on March 1 by between five and seven percent, said Buelens.
From Britain, rates went up 10 percent from April 1, the first rise for 18 months, according to UK country manager Bob Wetherill.
Buelens said he could not understand why carriers had decided to drop their fuel surcharges.
"We earn revenue in (Continental) European currencies and these have depreciated considerably against the dollar.", he said." - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706; Fax +5017
